artifacts.summary: Three-phase, 3-hour plan confined to the task directory: live-tree re-verification of probes 01-03 with axiom profiles, a fourth probe closing the quantified transposition sentence (qTrans_defines, statement type-checked at plan time), and a hand-off summary drafting the follow-up port task, the manuscript remark and the completeness notes.

user_decision.question: The research recommends two actions this task's contract forbids it from taking (no FormalSystem/ or manuscript edits): a ~400-line port of probes 01, 02 and 04 into the library, and a one-paragraph remark in the manuscript at sub:Conclusion. Should the port be opened as a follow-up lean4 task from the description Phase 3 drafts in the summary?
options: Open the follow-up port task from the drafted description once this task completes; apply the manuscript remark by hand
Leave both recommendations in the summary; open no follow-up task
user_decision.recommended: Open the follow-up port task from the drafted description once this task completes; apply the manuscript remark by hand

memory_candidates.content: When /orchestrate dispatches a plan for a verdict-first RESEARCH task whose description forbids library changes (file_scope confined to specs/{NNN}/probes and reports), the plan stays inside the task directory: (1) re-verify the research probes against source-rebuilt .oleans of their imported modules before trusting `lake env lean` exit 0, and pin axiom profiles on scratch copies; (2) close only the UNVERIFIED items that are routinely checkable with an additional probe whose statement is type-checked at plan time and pinned as the sole Lean Challenge identifier; (3) the report's recommendations that need FormalSystem/ or out-of-repo edits become a hand-off summary (ready-to-paste /task description with file_scope, remark text and placement) plus a non-blocking user_decision, never phases of this task. The port is a separate task with its own file_scope so lock-overlap detection against concurrent siblings holds.
